title: Is the subsample built at open still the right way to search with a max query length?
body:
`count`, `extract` and `locate` take `-m`/`--max-query-len`, which limits how many characters of a query a search compares. When the suffixes are opened in memory and that limit is shorter than the sort, `typed::open` in `libsufr/src/typed.rs` keeps the whole suffix array on disk and holds a subsample in memory instead. A search runs over the subsample and maps a hit back to ranks in the whole array.

The subsample is a `Subsample<W>`: the first suffix of each group that shares its first `max_query_len` characters, and that suffix's rank in the whole array. `TypedSuffixArray::subsample` builds it. With an LCP array it reads the LCP array in blocks and keeps a suffix whose LCP is below `max_query_len`. Without one, `subsample_by_text` calls `keep_differing`, which reads the suffix array in blocks and compares each suffix with the one before it, by the text or by the care positions under a seed mask. `subsample_with_cache` writes the result to `~/.sufr/locate-<max_query_len>-<basename>` and reads it back on a later open, unless the `.sufr` file is newer than the cache file.

Commit b3f9104 removed the build-time max query length, so an unmasked file is now always sorted on its full suffixes. `Header::sorted_len` is the text length for such a file, and any `-m` from 1 to below the text length on it now builds a subsample. The subsampling code was written when a capped build was the usual way to use `-m`, and nobody has reviewed it since that commit.

## Open

- Whether subsampling should stay at all. Building it reads every suffix and, without an LCP array, compares the text at each one. No one has timed that on a genome-sized file. The alternative is to search the whole array and stop comparing at `max_query_len`.
- Whether the in-memory subsample is worth the switch to a disk suffix array that the caller did not ask for. A caller who opens the suffixes in memory gets them on disk when `-m` is given.
- The cache key holds the file's basename and not its path, so two files with one name in different directories share a cache file. The mtime check guards only against a `.sufr` file newer than the cache.
- Whether a cache belongs in the library. Where it is written is sufr-22b9c3. The race on creating its directory, sufr-742f13, was fixed in 8f3d833, which creates the directory with `create_dir_all`.
- Which tests pin subsampled results against an unsubsampled search, with and without an LCP array and under a mask. `test_subsample_suffix_array` in `libsufr/src/lib.rs` checks the subsample itself.
